relations.evidence: Enables auto-failover when ephemeral buckets do not have replicas. If this happens then data loss can occur.

notable_absence.finding: The promoted registry's server:auto-failover concept states a default timeout of 120 seconds, but this CLI reference page never states any default value for --auto-failover-timeout at all - it only states the minimum allowed value per edition (30s Community, 5s Enterprise). A reader relying solely on this page would not learn what happens if --auto-failover-timeout is omitted from --set, which is a real documentation gap on the CLI's own reference page for the setting.

cross_component_finding: The promoted registry's server:auto-failover description compresses the timeout constraint to a single uniform 'range 5-3600 seconds,' but this page's actual text draws an edition-specific minimum distinction the registry's summary elides: 30 seconds is the floor in Community Edition, 5 seconds in Enterprise. This is a real precision gap between the condensed registry description and the CLI page's own edition-scoped detail - exactly the kind of terminology/precision drift this round is watching for, though here it's a registry-vs-source gap rather than a CLI-vs-REST/UI one. Otherwise 'automatic failover' / 'auto-failover' usage is consistent with the promoted term.
cross_product_finding: Not addressed on this page - no comparison to Capella, which manages failover automatically with no exposed auto-failover CLI configuration surface for customers.
